'''Charles F. Kennel''' (born August 20, 1939) is an American plasma [[physicist]] and former Associate Administrator of [[NASA]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11603002.html|title=Kennel, Charles F., 1939–|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ccst.us/ccstinfo/fellows/bios/kennel.php CCST Fellow Charles F. Kennel]</ref>  He is an elected member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" /> and won the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] in 1997.<ref name=":1" /> In 2009, he was advertised by [[NASA Watch]] as a potential pick by Barack Obama as the next [[NASA Administrator]].<ref>[http://www.nasawatch.com/archives/2009/01/the_force_is_st.html The Force Is Strong With This One]{{dead link|date=November 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ''[[NASA Watch]]'' January 9, 2009</ref>

==Early life and career==
Kennel received a bachelor's degree in astronomy from [[Harvard College]] and a doctorate in astrophysical sciences from [[Princeton University]]. His doctoral thesis was advised by [[Edward A. Frieman]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>[http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20040419/news_mz1b19biobyt.html Biobytes: Charles Kennel, Scripps Institution of Oceanography] ''[[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]''</ref>

Charles Kennel was a former Associate Administrator of [[NASA]]. He was the director of [[Mission to Planet Earth]], a program during the Clinton Administration to perform a comprehensive survey and observation of our home planet. He was a member and chair of the NASA Advisory Council (NAC) Science Committee which he quit in 2006.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141205221609/http://www.nbcnews.com/id/28566062/ More names mentioned for NASA post] ''[[NBC News]]'' By Brian Berger and Becky Iannotta</ref>

*Ninth Director of [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]]<ref>[http://www-chancellor.ucsd.edu/kennelqa.html Q&A with Charles Kennel, Scripps Institution of Oceanography] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070813195827/http://www-chancellor.ucsd.edu/kennelqa.html |date=August 13, 2007 }}</ref>
*Vice Chancellor of Marine Sciences at the [[University of California]], San Diego, from 1998 to 2006.
*Member and chair of the NASA Advisory Council  (1998–2006)
*Chair of the National Academy of Science's Space Studies Board<ref>[http://www.smartbrief.com/news/aia/storyDetails.jsp?issueid=E4B19040-6153-494E-A230-B6A4EEEA6F6C&copyid=D2E690C6-91CA-4F4F-9450-5F8827F829DD Obama wants scientist at NASA, sources say] [[SmartBrief]]</ref>
*In May 2009, Kennel was named a member of the [[Review of United States Human Space Flight Plans Committee]] an independent review requested by the [[Office of Science and Technology Policy]] (OSTP) on May 7, 2009.
*In January 2014, Kennel was elected the inaugural visiting research fellow at the [[Centre for Science and Policy]] (CSaP), University of Cambridge.<ref>[http://www.csap.cam.ac.uk/news/article-csap-welcomes-inaugural-visiting-research-fell/ CSaP welcomes inaugural Visiting Research Fellow]</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Kennel was awarded the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1987<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/charles-f-kennel/|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Charles F. Kennel|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> and was inducted into the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1991.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/charles-f-kennel-ofcwg6/|title=Charles Kennel|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> He was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Charles+F.+Kennel&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-08-31|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> In 1997, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Kennel&first_nm=Charles&year=1997|title=1997 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref>

==Works==

* Unstable growth of unducted whistlers propagating at an angle to the geomagnetic field – 1966 – Trieste : International Atomic Energy Agency, International Centre for Theoretical Physics
* What we have learned from the magnetosphere – 1974 – Los Angeles, Calif. : Plasma Physics Group, University of California, Los Angeles
* Matter in motion : the spirit and evolution of physics – 1977 – Charles F. Kennel and Ernest S. Abers – Boston : Allyn and Bacon
* Convection And Substorms: Paradigms Of Magnetospheric Phenomenology – 1996 – Oxford University Press, Usa – {{ISBN|0-19-508529-9}}
*[http://www.foreignaffairs.com/articles/137523/david-g-victor-charles-f-kennel-veerabhadran-ramanathan/the-climate-threat-we-can-beat The Climate Threat We Can Beat], in May/June 2012 Foreign Affairs with [[David G. Victor]], [[Veerabhadran Ramanathan]], and Kennel (website is paid while article is current)
